A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–F support reliable comparison. Bibliography reflow shifts the appendices by one page in v6 without removing material.

before.justification: v5 reports original SMC experiments in Section 5 and Appendices E–F, including normalizing-constant estimates, tuning costs, dimensional scaling, and backward-kernel comparisons.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices E–F, including benchmark comparisons and detailed adaptation diagnostics.

M1.justification: The greedy adaptation procedure, LMC/KLMC kernels, and Algorithms 1–8 are unchanged. The logarithm correction in Section 3.1 affects an intermediate derivation; the optimization objective and estimator in Equations (9)–(10) already appear unchanged in v5.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 22 benchmark problems listed in Tables 1–3 and the same Gaussian scenarios in Section 5.4 and Appendix E. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same fixed-parameter comparisons, differentiable AIS methods including End-to-End + VI, SMC-MALA-ESJD and SMC-MALA-ARC, and three backward-kernel alternatives.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B, E, and F retain the same evaluation metrics, particle budgets, annealing schedules, optimization settings, and testing procedures. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The dimensional-scaling experiment, backward-kernel analysis, adaptation-cost analysis, and temperature and step-size diagnostics are unchanged in Section 5.4 and Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Both retain 32 replications and 80% empirical quantiles for the main benchmark comparisons and Appendix F, and 256 replications for the backward-kernel comparison in Figure 7. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted curves, rankings, and reported findings match throughout Section 5 and Appendices E–F. This includes fixed-parameter comparisons, end-to-end optimization results, and adaptation diagnostics through Figure 37.

T1.justification: In Section 3.1 on page 4, v6 replaces the density-ratio integrand dQ/dP with log(dQ/dP) in the expansion of the incremental KL divergence. This corrects a local mathematical error. The assumptions, propositions, convergence guarantees, and Appendix D proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about greedy incremental KL adaptation, tuning without gradients, convergence guarantees, LMC/KLMC implementations, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the greedy scheme's lack of a guarantee of solving the joint optimization, poor performance on Rats, dimensional-scaling explanations, and the applicability limits of time-correct backward kernels.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices A–C retain the same implementation descriptions, preprocessing, hyperparameter tables, algorithm details, and code-access information. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to annealed flow transport, adaptive MCMC, and differentiable AIS are unchanged. The bibliography additions only identify the pages where existing works are cited.

P1.justification: v6 adds citation-page references to bibliography entries and updates the version/date stamp and internal page references. The main and appendix prose, terminology, section order, and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography page references alter line wrapping and page breaks, extending the references onto another page and shifting the contents and appendices. Figures, tables, captions, and their arrangements within corresponding pages remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 removes a local mathematical error by restoring the missing logarithm in the KL expansion on page 4. Citation-page references also improve navigation, with a modest increase in bibliography length. These are limited improvements; the algorithms, empirical evidence, claims, and limitations are unchanged.
